changesApplied.changeMade: Created complete state capture module with captureInitialState(), captureCurrentState(), computeDelta() functions
changesApplied.reason: Enables tracking of instructional → functional state transformations. Captures git commit/branch/dirty status, modified files, impulse IDs, working directory, and computes deltas between states.
keyFeatures: Non-blocking error handling - execution continues on state capture failure
Git state tracking via Snapshot.track() and Snapshot.diff() integration
Impulse delta detection - tracks impulses created during task execution
File change tracking - added/modified/deleted files with line counts

changesApplied.changeMade: Created HTTP client with storeActivityContent(), recordTaskStart(), updateTaskExecution() methods
changesApplied.reason: Enables persistence of activity execution data to backend API for learning loop. POSTs template_definition, variable_bindings, initial_state, reason, task_sequence to SurrealDB via Python backend.
keyFeatures: Non-blocking design - backend unavailability doesn't fail execution
Retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures
Configuration-based endpoint detection (activityBackend.url, metabob.apiUrl, env var)
Comprehensive payload schemas matching backend API contracts
Warning-level logging for debugging without noise

changesApplied.changeMade: Added 7 instrumentation points throughout activity execution lifecycle
changesApplied.reason: Closes the gap between frontend execution and backend persistence. Ensures every activity execution records complete context for learning loop.

impactAnalysis.blastRadius: High - core execution flow, but all changes non-blocking

Persist instructional state to backend API for learning loop

changesApplied.changeMade: Added Activity.save() call after each task completion (lines ~2552, ~2648)
changesApplied.reason: Fixes race condition where activity was saved once at end, losing task updates if concurrent executions or crashes occurred. Now saves incrementally after each task.
